end.summary:
Ishita practised showing growing sequences with coin and dot pictures.
They correctly built triangular-number rows: 1, 2, 3, 4, with total 10.
They used the shared-corner idea to explain why an added row and column do not double-count.
They correctly described the 6-by-6 to 7-by-7 growth as 7 + 6 = 13 dots.
Teach-back was not passed; no misconceptions were recorded.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised using pictures to show how a pattern grows and to explain why it is true. They used the shared-corner method correctly in the square examples, including explaining that the corner should not be counted twice. There was a brief double-counting mix-up with 13 and 12, which they corrected during the lesson. At home, ask them to draw a small square growing by one row and one column and label the shared corner.
